text: A song of ascents. Remember, LORD, on David's behalf, all the hardships he endured,

versions.text: A song of ascents. Remember, LORD, in David's favor all the hardships he endured,
versions.explanation: "in David's favor" is stiff and slightly ambiguous when read aloud; "on David's behalf" renders the dative לְדָוִד naturally and flows better for oral reading.

text: how he swore to the LORD and made this vow to the Mighty One of Jacob:
"I will not enter my house or lie down on my bed,
I will give no sleep to my eyes, no slumber to my eyelids,
until I find a place for the LORD, a dwelling for the Mighty One of Jacob."
We heard of it in Ephrathah; we found it in the fields of Jaar.^[Jaar is another name for Kiriath-jearim, the town where the ark of the covenant was kept for many years.]

versions.text: We heard of it in Ephrathah; we found it in the fields of Jaar.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew opens with הִנֵּה ("behold/indeed"), and "Jaar" will be opaque to hearers; a brief footnote identifying the place aids comprehension without altering the text.

text: Let us go to his dwelling place; let us worship at his footstool.
Rise up, LORD, and come to your resting place, you and the ark of your might.
May your priests be clothed with righteousness, and may your faithful ones shout for joy.
For the sake of David your servant, do not turn away the face of your anointed.
The LORD swore an oath to David, a sure oath he will not revoke: "One of your own descendants I will set on your throne.
If your sons keep my covenant and the decrees I teach them, then their sons also will sit on your throne forever."
For the LORD has chosen Zion; he has desired it for his dwelling:
"This is my resting place forever; here I will sit enthroned, for I have desired it.
I will richly bless her provisions; her poor I will satisfy with bread.
I will clothe her priests with salvation, and her faithful ones will sing aloud for joy.

versions.text: I will clothe her priests with salvation, and her faithful ones will shout for joy.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew uses an emphatic infinitive absolute construction (רַנֵּן יְרַנֵּנוּ), which is stronger than the plain verb used in verse 9; distinguishing the two keeps the intensification audible.

text: There I will make a horn grow for David; I have prepared a lamp for my anointed one.
I will clothe his enemies with shame, but on him the crown will shine."
